MUTUAL INDUCTANCE - Mutual inductance is the interaction of two inductors that are close to one another in a circuit. In other words, if the inductors are close enough, the magnetic field of one inductor produces a voltage in the other inductor and vice-versa. The amount of mutual inductance depends by how much of the magnetic fields of the two inductors interact.

The circuit increases and decreases the center frequency of the tank circuit according to the amplitude of the information signal which is FM.
Again, the amplitude of the negative information signal effects the amount of frequency change.
In other words, the information signal changed the output frequency modulation.
A lower capacitance in parallel to the tank circuit increases the resonant frequency.
The increased resistance lowers the capacitance of the R2, C3, and Q1 circuit.
If the information input signal is negative or decreasing, Q1 conducts less increasing its resistance.
The higher the positive amplitude of the information signal is the more Q1 conducts (decreasing resistance). More conduction from Q1causes more capacitance which decreases the output frequency.
In other words, the information signal changed the output frequency of the circuit, frequency modulation.
CAPACITANCE - Effect of capacitance in a tank circuit.
With more capacitance in parallel to the tank circuit, the resonant frequency decreases.
With more capacitance in parallel to the tank circuit, the resonant frequency decreases.
With decreased resistance, the capacitance of the R2, C3, and Q1 circuit increases.
This lowers the resistance of Q1 decreasing the resistance of the parallel circuit of R2, C3 and Q1.
With a positive or increasing information input signal, Q1 conducts.
This capacitance is added to the tank circuit of C7 and L2 producing a resonant frequency. This is the center frequency.
With Q1's resistance, the entire circuit appears as capacitive.
The reactance of C3 is large compared to the resistance of R2, which produces a capacitive circuit.
The resonant frequency of the tank circuit is determined by the values of C7, L2, R2, C3 and Q1.
The capacitance of R2, C3, and Q1 is in parallel to the oscillator's tank circuit C7 and L2 (the entire oscillator circuit is not shown).
Circuit operation is based on R2, C3, and Q1 appearing as a capacitive circuit.
